sections.title: Music in the Digital Age
sections.description: From the introduction of Napster to the disruption of the live music industry following the COVID-19 pandemic, the 21st century has seen profound transformations in how popular music is produced, performed, and consumed online. In this course, students will study the foundational concepts and categories that scholars of media and communication use to understand popular music. We will then examine several musical cultures and trends that have emerged online and explore different approaches to studying these phenomena. Finally, students will learn how to conduct their own research on digital music using ethnographic research techniques. Students will come away from this course with the ability to think and write clearly about popular music and its role in our digital world, as well as reflect on the role that digital music plays in their own lives. This course does not require any prerequisite knowledge of music theory or music history.
